text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The former deputy director of the Emergency Management Unit, Michael Ndivayele, has been reinstated as a civil servant even though he was convicted of fraud last year and having caused embarrassment to the government.
- The International Fund for Animal Welfare said Namibia's sealing industry was a "complete mess" after government officials last week confiscated seal meat from a company at Henties Bay.
- Sluices of Namibia's biggest reservoir, the Hardap Dam, have been partially opened as a precautionary measure to avoid flooding in the area along the Fish River.
- South African scientists have claimed a major breakthrough in the fight against AIDS.
- AIDS claimed 646 lives during 1996 in Namibia according to the National AIDS Control Programmes.
